title: Sevens: 5 and 2 More
goal: I can split 7 into 5 and 2 to find my 7s facts.

card.desc: Bristol learns ×7 = ×5 + ×2. She splits a 7-row array into 5 rows and 2 rows, finds each part with facts she knows, and adds (7 × 6 = 30 + 12 = 42). Today is hands-on: she builds and splits real arrays and sees a calendar as an array of 7s.

win: Sevens are no match for you. 5 and 2 more!

slides.title: Sevens: 5 and 2 More
slides.text: You split 7s with beans in class. Now do it on your own. 💪

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say each one out loud. Tell a grown-up if one is near.
prompts: How do you split a 7s fact?
Say the pattern: 5, 6, 7, 8. What does it mean?
What happened first in your book? What happened next?

slides.title: 5s part + 2s part
slides.text: Split the 7 into 5 and 2. Keep the other number.
slides.tip: Type your answer. You get 3 tries.

items.q: 7 × 9. The 5s part is 5 × 9 = 45. The 2s part is 2 × 9 = ____
Which shows 7 × 8?
items.why: Split the 7. Both parts are groups of 8: 40 + 16 = 56.
no: Both parts need groups of 8. 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 = 49. That is 7 × 7.

slides.title: Flower vases
slides.text: Marion has 7 vases. Each vase has 6 flowers. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each vase is one group. Set Groups to the number of vases. Set In each group to the flowers in one vase.

slides.title: Right split or wrong split?
slides.text: Check both parts. Then tap the box.
slides.done: Both parts use the same number. 7 × 6 = 5 × 6 + 2 × 6.

items.q: How many days are in 8 weeks? ____
How many days are in 3 weeks? ____
There are 7 dogs. Each dog has 4 legs. How many legs?
Amy has 7 apples. She gets 6 more. How many apples now?
items.why: Two amounts, not equal groups. Add: 7 + 6 = 13.
items.no: She gets more. Is that equal groups?

items.q: There are 7 boxes. Each box has 8 crayons. Do you multiply or add? Type multiply or add.
items.hint: Each box has 8. Same size groups.

sets.why: Split 7 into 5 and 2. Both parts are groups of 6.

sets.q: How many days are in 5 weeks? ____
There are 7 kids. Each kid has 6 crayons. How many crayons?
Marion has 7 marbles. Ellie has 9 marbles. How many in all?
no: These are two different amounts. Add.
2 is 9 − 7. The question asks how many in all.

sets.no: Flip it to 7 × 6. Then split the 7.

sets.why: Split the 7. Both parts are groups of 9: 45 + 18 = 63.
no: Both parts need groups of 9. 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 = 49. That is 7 × 7.

sets.q: How many days are in 2 weeks? ____
Liz has 7 fish tanks. Each tank has 5 fish. How many fish?
Amy has 7 pencils. Ellie has 7 pencils. How many pencils in all?
no: 49 is 7 × 7. There are only two 7s here: 7 + 7.
0 is 7 − 7. The question asks how many in all.

sets.q: One split has a mistake. Which one?

sets.why: Split the 7. Both parts are groups of 5: 25 + 10 = 35.
no: Both parts need groups of 5. 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 = 49. That is 7 × 7.

sets.q: How many days are in 7 weeks? ____
The vet has 7 rows of cages. Each row has 3 cages. How many cages?
Marion has 7 shells. She finds 5 more. How many shells now?
sets.why: Two amounts, not equal groups. Add: 7 + 5 = 12.
no: 35 is 7 groups of 5. She just found 5 more.

sets.q: Find the split that is not right.
Liz says 7 × 8 = 54. Type the right answer: 7 × 8 = ____

practice.intro: You get 3 tries on each one. Only your first try counts. For 7s: 5s part + 2s part.

no: 77 is 7 tens and 7 ones. 7 groups of 10 is 70.

questions.q: Each spider has 8 legs. How many legs on 7 spiders?

questions.why: Split 7 into 5 and 2. Both parts are groups of 4: 20 + 8 = 28.
no: Multiply each part. Do not add.

questions.q: How many days are in 6 weeks? ____
Amy walks the puppy 7 times. Each walk is 9 blocks. How many blocks?

no: 89 is 90 − 1. Take away a whole group of 9.

questions.q: Ellie has 7 pens. Liz has 8 pens. How many pens in all?
no: These are two different amounts. Add.
1 is 8 − 7. The question asks how many in all.

pages.title: Part 1: Split the 7

pages.title: Part 3: Days and weeks

teacher.objective: Bristol finds any 7s fact by splitting 7 into 5 and 2: she finds the 5s part and the 2s part (both facts she owns) and adds them (7 × 6 = 30 + 12 = 42). She sees the split in real arrays and in a calendar, and she keeps practicing yesterday's 8s and 9s tricks.
materials: The Class lesson open on your screen (teacher code)
About 70 beans or counters in two colors (or plain beans and a crayon to mark)
A long strip of paper or a ruler to split an array
Index cards: one 7s fact on each (7 × 3 to 7 × 9)
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Lesson 6 packet and Lesson 7 packet to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. Look at Monday's Show What You Know score. She says the 8s and 9s tricks.
Class slide 2. She retells in order with First, Next, Then. If she jumps around, ask: what happened before that?
Class slide 3. Before each tap, she names the trick.
Class slides 4–6. She builds 7 rows of 4 beans, ruler under row 5; she types the top part, bottom part and total (slide 5). Then 7 rows of 6 beans for slide 6.
Class slides 7–8. Bean piles for the puppy toys, then three taps. Say 5, 6, 7, 8 together.
Class slides 9–10. Ruler across the rows of 7 × 6: why 49 is wrong. Then the 7 × 9 steps in order, said aloud.
Class slides 11–12. She counts 4 weeks on the calendar page by rows, then types the days in 10 weeks and 9 weeks.

plan.block: Check the split and card flip
plan.do: Class slides 13–14. She checks each part on the whiteboard, then the 7s index cards: 5s part, 2s part, answer. Slow cards go aside for Thursday.
Class slide 15. She reads aloud and says equal groups or not before she taps.

Class slide 16. Read the two-night task list together: tonight the after-class lesson (with Show What You Know) and the Lesson 6 Practice; Wednesday the Lesson 7 Practice, the Lesson 6 packet and Lesson 7 packet page 1. Send both packets home.

watch: Using 7 in both parts: 7 × 6 as 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 (= 49, which is 7 × 7). Ask: which number tells the rows? Which tells how many in each row?
Writing the 2s part as just 2 (7 × 3 = 15 + 2). Point to the 2 rows: how many beans in each row?
Answering 49 in the ribbon problem (7 ribbons and 7 more). She multiplied because both numbers are 7. Ask: are there 7 equal groups, or just two amounts?

slides.title: Sevens: 5 and 2 More
slides.text: 7 is a tricky number. But 7 = 5 + 2. You know your 5s. You know your 2s. So you can do 7s! 💪

notes.do: Set out: beans (two colors if you have them), a ruler or paper strip, a calendar page, whiteboard, the 7s index cards. Collect last night's Show What You Know score from the course page.
notes.say: Yesterday you learned 8s and 9s. Today we beat the trickiest number: 7.
notes.listen: "8s: double the 4s. 9s: 10s take away one group." If she mixes them, say both again with 8 × 6 and 9 × 6 before you go on.

slides.title: Tell it in order
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy. Tell what happened in order.
prompts: What happened first in the part you read?
What do you think will happen at the end? Why?

notes.do: Book open. Let her look back at the pages she read.
notes.say: Tell me what happened, in order. Use First, Next, Then.
notes.ask: What happened before that? What happened after?
notes.listen: Events in the right order with time words. If she jumps around, ask: what happened before that? Then let her try again.

slides.title: 8s, 9s and 6s
slides.text: Use your tricks from last lesson and last week.

items.q: What is 8 × 7?
What is 9 × 6?
no: 51 is 60 − 9. Take away one group of 6.
59 is 60 − 1. Take away a whole group of 6.

items.q: What is 6 × 6?
no: 30 is 5 × 6. Add one more group of 6.

notes.ask: Which trick is this one: double the 4s, 10s take away a group, or 5s plus a group?
notes.listen: 8 × 7: double 28 is 56. 9 × 6: 60 − 6 = 54. 6 × 6: 30 + 6 = 36. If 7 × 8 = 54 shows up, fix it now with the double.

slides.title: Split the 7
slides.text: Here are 7 rows of 4. Let's split them into 5 rows and 2 rows.
slides.tip: 5 rows + 2 rows = 7 rows. You did not lose any!

notes.do: Before you click: she builds 7 rows of 4 beans on the table. Lay the ruler under row 5. Then click through the steps as she counts.
notes.say: 7 rows is 5 rows and 2 rows. You know 5s. You know 2s.
notes.ask: How many in the top part? In the bottom part? Together?
notes.listen: "20 and 8, so 28." Ask: did we lose any beans when we put the ruler down? (No: 5 rows + 2 rows = 7 rows.)

slides.title: Top part, bottom part
slides.text: Look at your beans. 7 rows of 4. Ruler under row 5.

items.q: The top part is 5 rows of 4. 5 × 4 = ____
The bottom part is 2 rows of 4. 2 × 4 = ____

items.why: Top part plus bottom part: 28. So 7 × 4 = 28.

notes.do: She types each answer herself (in person). Let her point to the beans as she answers.
notes.ask: Show me the top part. Show me the bottom part.
notes.listen: 20, 8, 28. If she types 9 for the top, she added 5 + 4. Point to the top part: 5 rows with 4 in each. Count it with her by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.

slides.title: Try 7 × 6
slides.tip: Both parts use the same number. For 7 × 6, it is 5 × 6 and 2 × 6.

notes.do: She builds 7 rows of 6 beans. Ruler under row 5 again.
notes.say: Same split. The 6 stays the same in both parts.
notes.ask: What is 5 × 6? What is 2 × 6? Put them together.
notes.listen: "30 and 12 is 42." Wrong: 35 + 14 = 49 (she used 7 in both parts, which is 7 × 7). Point: how many beans in each row? 6, in both parts.

slides.title: Puppy toys
slides.text: There are 7 puppies. Each puppy gets 3 toys. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each puppy is one group. Set Groups to the number of puppies. Set In each group to the toys for one puppy.

notes.do: She sets out 7 piles of 3 beans first, then taps the + buttons to match.
notes.ask: How many puppies? How many toys for each? Now split: 5 piles and 2 piles.

no: 48 is 6 × 8. You need one more group of 8.

items.q: What is 7 × 7?
no: 42 is 6 × 7. You need one more group of 7.

items.q: Which shows 7 × 3?
items.why: Split the 7. Both parts are groups of 3: 15 + 6 = 21.
no: The 2 rows also have 3 in each. It is 2 × 3, not 2.
Both parts need groups of 3. 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 = 49. That is 7 × 7.

notes.say: Say both parts out loud. Then tap.
notes.ask: For 7 × 8: what is 5 × 8? 2 × 8? Now say it with me: 5, 6, 7, 8. 56 = 7 × 8.
notes.listen: "40 and 16 is 56." If she picks 54, say the 5, 6, 7, 8 pattern together and write it on the whiteboard.

slides.title: Split the 7. Keep the other number.
slides.text: For 7 × 6, split the 7. The 6 stays in both parts.

steps.text: ❌ Not 5 × 7 and 2 × 7. That makes 35 + 14 = 49. That is 7 × 7!

slides.tip: Ask: how many rows? How many in each row? Only the rows get split.

notes.do: Build 7 rows of 6 again. Lay the ruler across the rows, never down a row.
notes.say: The ruler only splits the rows. Every row still has 6.
notes.listen: "Because each row has 6, not 7." or "49 is 7 × 7." Either shows she sees it.

slides.title: How to do 7 × 9
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
slides.hint: First split the 7. Then find both parts.

notes.say: Say each step out loud before you tap it.
notes.ask: What comes first: split, find parts, or add?
notes.listen: Split, 45 and 18, add to 63. If she starts with adding, ask: add what? We need the parts first.

slides.title: A calendar is an array!
slides.text: A week has 7 days. Each row on a calendar is one week.

steps.text: How many days in 4 weeks? That is 4 rows of 7.
4 × 7 is the same as 7 × 4. We know that one: 28!

slides.tip: A turn-around fact has the same answer. 4 × 7 = 7 × 4.

notes.do: Hand her the calendar page. She counts the days in the first 4 rows (weeks).
notes.say: Every row on a calendar is one week: 7 days. A calendar is an array of 7s!
notes.ask: How many rows did you count? How many in each row? So which fact is it?
notes.listen: "4 rows of 7, 4 × 7 = 28." Then she flips it: 7 × 4 = 28 too.

items.q: How many days are in 10 weeks? ____
How many days are in 9 weeks? ____
items.hint: 10 weeks is 70. Take away one week.

notes.ask: Which trick did you use for 9 weeks?
notes.listen: Either works: 10s take away one group (70 − 7) or split the 7 (45 + 18). Praise her for choosing.

items.q: Liz writes 7 × 3 = 15 + 2. What is wrong?
no: Split the 7. The 5s part is 5 × 3 = 15. That part is right.

items.q: Ellie writes 7 × 8 = 40 + 14. What is wrong?
Which split is right for 7 × 5?
no: 35 is the answer, not the 5s part. 5 × 5 = 25.

notes.do: She checks each part on the whiteboard before she taps.
notes.ask: Check the 5s part. Is it right? Now check the 2s part.
notes.listen: She finds which part is wrong, not just that it is wrong.

slides.title: Say both parts
slides.text: I flip a card. You say the 5s part, the 2s part, and the answer. Then we check the hard ones here.

steps.text: Cards first. Then click to check these four.

slides.tip: 5s part + 2s part. Same number in both parts.

notes.do: Use the 7s index cards (7 × 3 to 7 × 9), shuffled. She says both parts and the answer for each card. Put any slow card aside for Thursday. After the cards, click through the steps to check 7 × 3, 7 × 7, 7 × 8 and 7 × 9 together.
notes.say: Fast is good. Right is better. Say both parts every time.
notes.listen: Both parts, then the total. If she skips the parts and guesses, ask for the parts again.

items.q: Amy walks the puppy every day for 3 weeks. How many days is that?
no: 10 is 3 + 7. Each week has 7 days, so multiply.

items.q: Liz has 7 jars. She puts 6 biscuits in each jar. How many biscuits?
no: 13 is 7 + 6. Each jar has 6, so multiply.

items.q: Ellie has 7 ribbons. Marion gives her 7 more. How many now?
items.why: This is one group plus another. Add: 7 + 7 = 14.
no: Two 7s is not 7 groups of 7. Add them.

notes.say: Before you tap: equal groups or not?
notes.ask: For the ribbons: are there 7 equal groups, or just two amounts?
notes.listen: Weeks and jars are equal groups: multiply. "7 ribbons and 7 more" is two amounts: add (14). If she says 49, she multiplied because both numbers are 7.
